tasks.description: Persist the uploaded-file list the same way chat history is already persisted, and restore it on startup the same way chat history is already restored. Add UPLOADED_FILES_PATH = "data/uploaded_files.json" to backend/config.py. In backend/services/state.py::AppState, first extract the JSON read/write boilerplate that save_history()/load_history() already duplicate into private helpers (e.g. _save_json(path, data) writing data as JSON to path and creating the parent dir if needed, and _load_json(path, default) returning default if the file is missing or on read error), and refactor save_history()/load_history() to use them. Then add save_files()/load_files() built on the same helpers: save_files() fully replaces (not appends) the JSON file's contents with the current state.loaded_files; load_files() reads UPLOADED_FILES_PATH into state.loaded_files if the file exists, and leaves state.loaded_files as [] (no error, no file created) if it doesn't. Wire these into backend/services/ingestion.py: in ingest(), call app_state.save_files() right after app_state.loaded_files is set. In restore(), after the existing FAISS-index restore attempt, call app_state.load_files() to repopulate app_state.loaded_files from disk; if the FAISS index failed to load (the existing except branch), clear app_state.loaded_files to [] instead of loading from disk, so the list never claims files are available when the index isn't usable. Include unit tests covering: save_files()/load_files() round-trip and replace (not append) semantics; load_files() leaves loaded_files empty with no error when the file is absent; existing chat-history save/load behavior is unchanged after the helper extraction; after ingest() + restore() (simulating a restart), loaded_files reflects the previously uploaded filenames; a fresh restore() with nothing ever uploaded leaves loaded_files empty with no error; when FAISS index restore fails, loaded_files ends up empty even if uploaded_files.json has stale content.
